summary:
AQUABOTS MAX ECOSYSTEM is an integrated environmental monitoring system designed to improve the observation and understanding of water quality in coastal lagoons and other aquatic ecosystems.

The project combines autonomous IoT monitoring stations, real-time physicochemical measurements, cloud-based data processing, and NASA Earth observation resources to support science-based environmental decision-making.

Its monitoring infrastructure measures water temperature, pH, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, salinity, and oxidation-reduction potential, alongside estimated environmental indicators.

Satellite observations, including Landsat-derived surface temperature and water indices, provide additional spatial and temporal context. These data complement in-situ measurements through interactive maps and environmental dashboards.

Initially developed around Laguna de Tres Palos in Guerrero, Mexico, AQUABOTS aims to strengthen environmental research, community participation, and early awareness of conditions that may threaten aquatic ecosystems.

The project demonstrates how space technology and affordable monitoring systems can work together to make environmental information more accessible and actionable.
details:
Project Details – NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1. Project Overview

AQUABOTS MAX ECOSYSTEM is an integrated technological platform for remote, near-real-time monitoring of physicochemical water quality in coastal lagoons and aquatic ecosystems.

The project combines autonomous Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring stations, environmental sensors, satellite Earth observations, cloud infrastructure, and geospatial visualization to support environmental research and socio-environmental decision-making.

Our initial implementation focuses on Laguna de Tres Palos in Guerrero, Mexico, where continuous environmental monitoring is essential for understanding changes in aquatic conditions.

2. The Environmental Challenge

Coastal lagoons are exposed to environmental pressures associated with changing temperatures, precipitation patterns, human activities, and variations in water conditions.

Traditional monitoring often relies on occasional field sampling, which can leave significant gaps in environmental information.

AQUABOTS addresses this challenge by combining continuous local measurements with satellite observations, providing a more comprehensive perspective of aquatic ecosystems.

The project is particularly relevant to areas experiencing environmental stress and fish mortality events, where timely and reliable observations are essential.

3. How AQUABOTS Works

The system integrates four technological layers.

Layer 1 – Autonomous Monitoring Stations

AQUABOTS stations use ESP32 microcontrollers and environmental sensors to collect physicochemical measurements.

The system includes:

  • Water temperature
  • pH
  • Total dissolved solids (TDS)
  • Electrical conductivity
  • Salinity
  • Oxidation-reduction potential (ORP)

Additional indicators, including dissolved oxygen and carbon dioxide, are currently estimated from available measurements and computational relationships rather than obtained from dedicated direct-measurement sensors.

Stationary devices transmit readings approximately every five minutes through MQTT communication.

Layer 2 – Satellite Earth Observation

AQUABOTS incorporates satellite-derived environmental information to complement in-situ measurements.

NASA-related resources include:

  • Landsat surface temperature observations for evaluating thermal conditions.
  • Landsat-derived Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) for analyzing surface-water characteristics.
  • NASA GPM IMERG precipitation information for understanding rainfall conditions.
  • MODIS-derived optical observations for additional aquatic environmental context.

The project also explores NISAR synthetic aperture radar observations as a future complementary capability.

Satellite data provide regional context that cannot be obtained through individual monitoring stations alone.

Layer 3 – Data Infrastructure and Processing

Measurements are transmitted to a centralized infrastructure for storage, processing, and consultation.

The system uses:

  • ESP32 embedded hardware
  • MQTT communication
  • Python and Flask services
  • MySQL database infrastructure
  • REST-based data services
  • Web technologies for environmental visualization

Historical measurements and satellite observations support environmental summaries, statistical relationships, and analysis across different time periods.

Layer 4 – Environmental Dashboard

The public monitoring platform provides access to environmental observations through interactive visualizations.

The dashboard includes:

  • Recent physicochemical measurements
  • Historical environmental data
  • Satellite information layers
  • Geographic visualization
  • Temporal comparisons
  • Environmental statistics and analytical summaries

The public platform is available at:

https://monitoreo.trespalos.org

4. Innovation and Creativity

AQUABOTS combines two complementary observation methods: direct in-situ environmental sensing and space-based Earth observation.

Its main innovation is the integration of relatively affordable autonomous monitoring equipment with satellite environmental information in a single accessible ecosystem.

This approach bridges the gap between local field measurements and wider geographical observations.

The project emphasizes technological accessibility, reproducibility, scientific interpretation, and practical applications for communities.

5. Current Progress and Improvements

The project has developed operational monitoring equipment, data communication infrastructure, database services, and a public environmental dashboard.

Its ongoing improvements include:

  • Expanding the geographic coverage of monitoring stations.
  • Strengthening sensor calibration and field validation.
  • Improving comparison between local measurements and satellite observations.
  • Evaluating additional radar-based observations.
  • Developing more robust environmental reporting tools.
  • Improving energy autonomy and deployment durability.
  • Advancing analytical methods for environmental interpretation.

These improvements are part of the project roadmap and should not be confused with fully deployed capabilities.

6. Benefits and Expected Impact

Environmental Impact

AQUABOTS supports continuous observation of water conditions and helps identify changes that may require further scientific investigation.

Scientific Impact

The system creates opportunities to compare ground-based observations with satellite environmental datasets across different spatial and temporal scales.

Social Impact

Accessible information can help local communities, researchers, and institutions participate in discussions about aquatic ecosystem conservation.

Educational Impact

The project demonstrates practical applications of electronics, IoT communication, programming, environmental science, and NASA Earth observation technologies.

Technological Impact

AQUABOTS provides an adaptable foundation for developing low-cost monitoring networks in additional aquatic environments.

7. Why NASA Earth Observations Matter

NASA Earth observation resources strengthen AQUABOTS by providing environmental context beyond the physical location of its sensors.

Satellite-derived temperature, surface-water indicators, precipitation, and optical observations can help researchers interpret broader environmental conditions.

Combining these resources with local monitoring creates a more informative foundation for understanding aquatic ecosystems.

AQUABOTS demonstrates how NASA scientific data can be translated into accessible environmental tools with potential benefits for communities, education, and research.

8. Future Vision

Our long-term vision is to develop a scalable environmental monitoring ecosystem capable of supporting multiple lagoons and aquatic environments.

Future efforts will emphasize scientific validation, reliable field instrumentation, regional deployment, advanced data analysis, and stronger collaboration with environmental institutions.

AQUABOTS MAX ECOSYSTEM seeks to connect autonomous environmental monitoring, space-based observations, and community knowledge to support sustainable management of aquatic ecosystems.

AQUABOTS MAX ECOSYSTEM – Connecting Water, Earth Observation, Technology, and Communities.
